questions.prompt: Closes are 106, 103 and 99 on three days in a row. What does the 3-bar trend rule give on the third day?
options: +1, because the average of 102.67 is above 99
0, because the close of 99 is below the average of 102.67
0, because there is not enough history
questions.explanation: The moving average is (106 + 103 + 99) / 3 = 102.67. The rule gives +1 only when the close is above its average, and 99 is below it, so the signal is 0.

questions.prompt: You compute a signal for 2025-03-07 twice: once with all 10 bars and once with bars up to 2025-03-07. The two values differ. What does that tell you?
options: The moving average window is too short
pandas sorted the bars in a different order
The rule used bars after 2025-03-07, so it reads the future
The signal is working as intended
questions.explanation: A signal may use only the data known up to its bar. If later bars change an earlier value, the rule read them, and a replay would trade on information nobody had then.

questions.prompt: On 2025-03-13 the close is 101 and its 3-bar moving average is 101.00. Why is the signal 0?
options: Because the rule needs the close to be strictly above the average, and a tie is not above
Because the average is missing on that day
Because the close fell from the day before
Because the signal can change at most twice
questions.explanation: The code tests `closes > average`. Equal values make that test false, so this rule treats a tie as no view and gives 0.
